newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London dip on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London dip on profit-taking.

text.p: U.S. stocks trading in London were slightly lower across the board as European investors decided to take some profits after the Dow's second straight record close on Monday.
"Today we're seeing a bit of profit-taking in the absence of any major corporate news," said one trader. "It is purely technical, the market is looking in remarkably good shape."
The Dow on Monday climbed 42.72 points to 7478.5, more than 1,000 points higher than it started the year. Technology and drug stocks were lifted by the weaker dollar.
In London, Eli Lilly & Co came under pressure from profit-takers and was down $1/2 at $99-3/4. Pfizer Inc shed $3/8 to $108-1/8.
Dealers said some hi-tech stocks also slipped from recent highs. "But they are again just reflecting recent gains," one said.
Intel fell $5/8 to $148-5/8 after bouncing from the lows.
"Bonds are fractionally firmer and futures are unchanged so based on what we've seen in Europe this morning, the opening (in New York) should be around 10 points lower," one trader said.
